answer.why_different: The generated side omits the entire callback structure, likely because the notification callback was not mapped from the 3GPP notification to an OpenAPI callback expression and POST Path Item. This is a structural omission that also removes the callback address, request body, and responses.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification requires notifyMOIAttributeValueChanges to be mapped to an HTTP POST at the notification target. Its notification type is NotifyMoiAttributeValueChanges, and a successful response has no body with errors represented by ErrorResponse.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 supports callbacks as a map of callback objects, where each callback expression identifies the runtime URL for the callback. The expression value must contain a Path Item Object describing the callback request and expected responses.
answer.clearer_why: The official version exposes the callback target, POST operation, required notification payload, and success/error responses. The generated version provides no callback definition, so a reader cannot discover or understand this notification interaction from the API document.

```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)

The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
